Jon Rahm: How DP World Tour win in Abu Dhabi marks start of 'next page' in career after mental strain of LIV Golf exit
Jon Rahm opened up about the arrival of his fourth child and the challenges of his LIV Golf League exit after his Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship win - his sixth Rolex Series victory and first DP World Tour title since The Masters in April 2023
Sunday 8 November 2026 16:35, UK
Jon Rahm has experienced plenty of change on - and off - the golf course in recent months, with the Spaniard pleased to begin the "next page" of his career with a victory.
Rahm returned from a seven-week absence to make his debut at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship, where a two-shot win marked his 11th DP World Tour title and his first since April 2023.
The Rolex Series event was his first start since finishing rock-bottom at September's BMW PGA Championship, where Rahm's mind was focused primarily on the possibility of his impending fourth child arriving early.
Rahm's wife Kelley welcomed their daughter Begona in mid-October and the Spaniard's playing future has also since been made clearer, having made a separation agreement with LIV Golf ahead of them 'winding down operations'.
The former world No 1 failed to win on the DP World Tour during his three seasons with LIV Golf, but victory over Ryder Cup teammates Tyrrell Hatton and Rory McIlroy is a record sixth Rolex Series victory.
"It [winning] means a lot," Rahm said. "It's been quite a while since I've played good in a DP World Tour event. From last [BMW PGA Championship] to first is a pretty good feeling."
He added: "To battle it out with Tyrrell [Hatton], who is the other man with five [Rolex Series wins], to break the tie and get it done - he's a good friend of mine and I know how good a competitor he is. It's a special week."
Rahm's attorney told a bankruptcy court last month that he would not be participating with any proposed 'LIV 2.0', having topped the individual standings in all three seasons on the circuit and won four of their events.
He has faced regular questions about his - and the league's future - throughout the season, although can now turn his attention to featuring more frequently on the DP World Tour.
"Whether you like to admit it or not, it [LIV Golf] was a lot of extra noise going on in general, and that was still not the most important part of my life," he said.
"In the sense of the impending birth of our daughter was something that was weighing heavily on me at Wentworth, I'm not going to lie, I didn't want to miss it. It was a little bit more difficult to perhaps play and think throughout the golf course [when] it felt a little bit cloudy in a sense.
"The calmness I felt this week has been enjoyable all week, honestly. I felt incredible calm, even when things didn't go anyway. Not much seemed to bother me, and probably the main reason why I was able to perform the way I have."
On whether the demise of LIV Golf marked the end of one chapter of his career, Rahm said: "One could say that.
"After everything that's gone on, and some poor play and some battles mentally with a lot of noise, to come back out after a bit of rest and having a new addition to the family, it's quite special."
Could Rahm still win the Race to Dubai?
Rahm said pre-tournament that he not talked with the PGA Tour about a potential return, while his win in Abu Dhabi keeps his hopes alive of winning the DP World Tour's Race to Dubai this season.
"I don't know how else to say it - it's on to the next page, right," Rahm explained. "Luckily in golf, I've been fortunate to have a lot of opportunities and take advantage of them.
"Hopefully I can keep doing so."
Rahm is one of nine players now with a mathematical chance of winning the Race to Dubai, although needs to win the DP World Tour Championship for a fourth time and require both Eugenio Chacarra and Rory McIlroy's results to go in his favour.
"I didn't think I would ever have a chance to win it [Race to Dubai]," Rahm added. "I'm very excited - it actually gives me a little extra incentive next week.
"Those are better odds than I expected so looking forward to it and hopefully I can get my fourth one [DP World Tour Championship]."
What's next?
The DP World Tour season reaches its climax next week at the DP World Tour Championship, where only the top 50 available players in the Race to Dubai standings are eligible to compete.

שחקן הגולף הספרדי ג'ון ראם פתח לדבריו "עמוד חדש" בקריירה שלו לאחר שזכה באליפות אבו דאבי, שהיא הניצחון הראשון שלו בסבב אירופי מאז אפריל 2023. הניצחון הגיע לאחר תקופה סוערת שכללה עזיבה של ליגת LIV Golf, התמודדות עם מתחים נפשיים, והולדת בתו הרביעית בחודש שעבר עם רעייתו קלי.

הזכייה באבו דאבי מסמלת את תוארו ה-11 במספר בסבב ומציבה אותו בין המועמדים הבודדים שיכולים עדיין לזכות במירוץ לדובאי לעונת זו. ראם הביע שביעות רצון מהשקט הנפשי שהרגיש במהלך הטורניר, בניגוד לרעשי הרקע והלחצים שליוו אותו בחודשים האחרונים לפני פרישתו הסופית מהסבב הקודם.
